Carrier adapters · data model · admin tab contribution

Carriers are the new PSPs.
One CarrierAdapterInterface, N implementations.

Carrier abstraction · mirrors PaymentAdapter
interface CarrierAdapterInterface
{
    public function quoteRate(QuoteRateRequest $r): RateResponse;
    public function createShipment(ShipmentRequest $r): ShipmentResponse;
    public function cancelShipment(string $trackingNumber): bool;
    public function trackShipment(string $trackingNumber): TrackingStatus;

    public function getCarrierName(): string;
    public function getSupportedCountries(): array;
    public function supportsFeature(string $feature): bool;
}

// 3 concrete impls behind a registry, picked by config + region
class DhlAdapter   implements CarrierAdapterInterface { /* … */ }
class UpsAdapter   implements CarrierAdapterInterface { /* … */ }
class FedExAdapter implements CarrierAdapterInterface { /* … */ }

// Tagged registry — same SOLID pattern as PSPs
CarrierAdapterRegistry:
    arguments:
      - !tagged_iterator shipping.carrier_adapter
DhlAdapter:
    tags: [{ name: shipping.carrier_adapter, region: EU }]
Where data lives
  • Tracking number. On the contract via $contract->setMetadata('tracking_number', …) — queryable on the order detail page without a join.
  • Shipment record. Module’s own table (oe_shipping_shipment) keyed on contract ID. Survives the contract.
  • Carrier choice / rate / SLA. Module’s table (oe_shipping_quote). Linked to BasketSnapshot hash for reproducibility.
  • Audit trail. Reuse oe_payments_transaction for shipping events — or your own table if domain-distinct.
Admin tab · contribute, don’t replace
class ShippingPanelProvider implements PanelProviderInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ShipmentRepository $repo,
        private readonly TrackingNumberService $tracking,
    ) {}

    public function supports(Order $order): bool
    {
        return $this->repo->existsByOrderId($order->getId());
    }

    public function render(Order $order): PanelView
    {
        return new PanelView(
            title: 'Shipment',
            template: '@shipping/panel.html.twig',
            data: [
                'shipment' => $this->repo->findByOrder($order),
                'tracking' => $this->tracking->urlFor($order),
            ]
        );
    }
}

# services.yaml
ShippingPanelProvider:
    tags:
      - { name: oe.payment.admin_panel,
          provider: shipping, priority: 50 }
What’s on the panel
  • Carrier name, label PDF download link, tracking number with click-through
  • Last known status from trackShipment() (cached for 5 min)
  • Action buttons: cancel shipment, regenerate label, mark as delivered (admin override)
  • Cost, SLA, weight, dimensions — what the carrier returned at quote time
One tab. Every consumer. Payment Base’s “Payment” tab now hosts: PSP panel(s), OpalReturns panel, Shipping panel. Each is a tagged service. Adding a 5th panel is one YAML entry.
